entry.title: v0.9.75
entry.content:
Intra-class call binding across five languages, new language-structure coverage, and a batch of resolution/build/cache fixes.

  • Feature: self/this/super member calls now bind to the caller's own class chain instead of the file-wide last-definition, across Python (self./cls./super(), nearest ancestor in the in-file MRO) (#4011), JavaScript/TypeScript (this.m() to the caller's own class; super.m() fails closed since the extends chain is not known at that pass) (#4012), Swift (self/super, class vs struct/extension aware) (#4030), and Ruby (self-sends within the class chain, complementing the paren-less self-send extraction from 0.9.74) (#4031) — all thanks @Cintu07. Multiple-inheritance ties and unknown/external ancestors fail closed (no fabricated edge).
  • Feature: four more language extractors gained structural coverage from @rajatnagda45 — Zig error-set declarations and their members (case_of) (#4025), PHP enum cases (pure and backed) with case_of edges (#4026), Elixir defmacro/defmacrop/defguard/defguardp definitions (#4027), and Rust macro_rules! definitions with local invocation resolution (std macros like println! fail closed, no fabrication) (#4028).
  • Feature: three Scala type-reference fixes from @Faisal-Fayaz — file-scope val/var type annotations now emit references edges (#4036, #2054), type alias/definition right-hand sides are walked (including opaque type and match types) (#4037, #2049), and context bounds (def f[A: Ordering]) resolve to references edges (#4038, #2046).
  • Feature: single-implementer interface dispatch was lifted into a language-agnostic core (#4034) and reused to dispatch a Swift protocol requirement to its sole conformer (INFERRED), failing closed on 2+ conformers (#4035) — thanks @GAURAV-1313.
  • Feature: Elixir unqualified calls now resolve to functions brought in by import/use, scoped per module and fail-closed when no in-scope module defines the name (fixes a large god-node from corpus-wide bare-name binding) (#4015, thanks @Ayushraj06-bit).
  • Feature: a bash script's invocation of another script through a non-shell interpreter (python3 build.py, node build.js, "$PYTHON" stage.py) is now recorded as an invokes edge; a $VAR/path command word is not mistaken for an interpreter (#4007, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Feature: Dart part files keep their own file node linked to the library (#4013, #4008), and a configurable import/export (import 'a.dart' if (...) 'b.dart';) now links every URI branch, not just the default (#4003, #4002) — thanks @brlumen.
  • Fix: C# partial-class merging no longer drops recursive/intra-class calls edges; one split partial class anywhere in a repo used to erase every recursive self-loop graph-wide (#4017, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
  • Fix: graphify path (CLI and the MCP shortest_path tool) now routes through a contains edge back out to a symbol's file, so a cross-file dependency that must pass through a shared symbol is found instead of reporting no path (#4004, #3878, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: the AST cache rebinds its stat index when a later call names a different cache root, so a multi-project process writes each root's stat-index.json with only its own files instead of pooling them into the first root's file (#4005, #3989, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: merge-graphs --previous <merged-graph.json> restores the previous merged community assignment by node id, so cluster/label reuse stays stable across re-merges; a malformed --previous file now errors cleanly instead of crashing (#4006, #3858, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: cluster-only/label no longer drop parallel edges (two different relations between the same pair) when reloading and rewriting a graph; preserved links track node-id remaps so none are silently dropped on a legacy graph (#4010, #3999, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: the Ollama num_ctx setting is merged into extra_body instead of replacing it, so a GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING body set on the same backend is no longer silently clobbered (#4029, #3988, thanks @Agnik47).
  • Fix: the hook-guard reminder names the effective graph.json path when GRAPHIFY_OUT is customized, instead of always naming the default graphify-out/graph.json (#4042, #4040, thanks @DeepanshuPal).
  • Fix: graphify extract refuses to overwrite an existing graph with a dedup-shrunk one unless --allow-dedup-shrink is passed; the refusal reports the actual number of nodes dedup merged (#4014, #3774, thanks @SrijanSriv).
  • Feature: extraction warns once when a cleanly-parsed code file yields no symbols beyond its own file node (often a data literal), while staying silent on empty/whitespace-only files, no-extractor languages, and intentionally-skipped data (#4009, #3946, thanks @ayushcodes10).

entry.title: [261004] How Macs Save Power: Slipping in 6 Efficiency Cores
entry.content:
TLDR

  • Heterogeneous Architecture: Apple Silicon uses P-cores and E-cores in tandem, offloading low-power tasks to E-cores to drastically boost Mac battery life.
  • Core Evolution: Starting with M4/M5, base chips upgraded to 6 E-cores (4P + 6E), while Pro/Max/Ultra models stack P-cores for peak performance.
  • x cpu Type Identification: x-cmd v0.10.9 adds P/E core identification and idle stats to x cpu, showing real-time core workload distribution.

entry.title: Desktop app improvements, agent comment replies, and more
entry.content:
Desktop app

  • Deep links: mintlify:// links open in the desktop app as a new tab.
  • Zoom and new tabs: Zoom in, zoom out, or reset the zoom from the View menu. Cmd + N opens a new tab with a blank page.
  • Offline screen: Navigation changes you made while offline save when your connection returns. The app shows an offline screen if you lose your connection.
  • Find in page: Press Cmd + F to search the current page. See Keyboard shortcuts for more information.
  • Check for updates: Check for a new version from the app menu or settings. See Updates for more information.
  • Browser sign-in: Sign in to the desktop app through your default browser. If browser sign-in isn't available for your organization, sign in inside the app. See Sign in for more information.

Agent and AI

  • Agent replies to comments: The agent can read open comments and suggestions on a page, reply to threads, and resolve comment threads.
  • Google Docs integration: Connect Google Docs as a read-only personal integration so the agent can search and read your documents. Available on Enterprise plans.
  • Admin MCP: The admin MCP can edit your deploy branch directly when the branch doesn't require pull requests. It can also upload images and returns links to private pages. The diff shows who made each pending change.
  • Group-scoped MCP credentials: Assign user groups to MCP client credentials so they can access pages restricted to those groups. You can't change a credential's groups after you create it.
  • Custom skills on authenticated sites: Skills marked public: true appear for visitors who aren't signed in. See Share skills on authenticated sites.
  • Multiple pull requests per automation run: Custom automations can open several pull requests in one run, or add commits to a pull request that an earlier run opened. See Open multiple pull requests or append to open ones.

Editor and dashboard

  • Images in the editor: Click an image to select it. Drag it to move it, even inside frames, cards, tabs, and callouts, and resize it with handles that also work on touch screens. Dropped and pasted media lands between blocks.
  • Emoji reactions on text: Highlight text and react to it with an emoji. See Comments.
  • Publish warnings: The Publish menu warns you about open comments and labels unlisted pages as hidden.
  • Fewer confirmations: Source mode asks you to confirm a large change only when it exceeds 10,000 characters.
  • Keyboard shortcuts in the editor: Open Keyboard shortcuts from the dashboard help menu to see every shortcut. See View shortcuts in the dashboard for more information.
  • Starting page: Choose which dashboard page opens first. See Starting page for more information.
  • Preview access: Switch an existing preview between dashboard login and password protection. When you turn on authentication, choose whether to keep existing previews, delete public previews, or delete all previews. See Restrict access to preview deployments for more information.

Published sites and deployments

  • Page modes in every theme: Every theme supports center and frame page modes. In Maple and Almond, center mode keeps the sidebar and centers the content beside it. See Page mode for more information.
  • Endpoint frontmatter validation: Deployments fail if a page's api, openapi, or asyncapi frontmatter is a list instead of a single endpoint string, such as "GET /users".

Bug fixes

  • Editor: Ordered lists keep their numbering when you delete an empty middle item. Any block now renders between accordions in an AccordionGroup. Images pasted from other sites stay on the page. Source mode parses MDX import and export blocks correctly.
  • Private pages: Moving a private page to your site keeps its page ID and comments. Private pages load regardless of Git branch state.
  • Published sites: Images in table cells are zoomable. API playground requests without a body no longer send a Content-Type header. Search breadcrumbs match the page language. Willow renders custom page mode.
  • Assistant: The assistant widget on sites without authentication searches every page, not only pages marked public: true.
  • Authenticated sites: Generated OG images and PDF exports work on sites with authentication.
  • Previews: GitLab multi-repo preview deployments work, failed merge request comments no longer fail preview builds, and retargeting a pull request to your deploy branch creates a preview.
  • Agent: The editor agent uses your timezone.
  • Analytics: CSV exports escape spreadsheet formulas.
  • CLI: The CLI accepts AsyncAPI 3.0.0 specs on fresh installs.

entry.title: v0.9.74
entry.content:
• Feature: four more language extractors gained structural depth. Ruby paren-less self-sends (do_thing with no receiver or parens) are now captured as calls, with a local-variable/parameter/block-parameter in scope correctly suppressing the call (fail-closed, no fabrication) (#3960, thanks @rajatnagda45). TypeScript abstract method signatures in an abstract class are now extracted as callable method members and resolve as call targets (#3961, thanks @rajatnagda45). Scala deferred (abstract) method declarations in traits and abstract classes (def foo: Int, no body) are now extracted as methods (#3962, thanks @rajatnagda45). C++ a member-function declaration inside a class (void foo();, defined out-of-line) is now classified as a method rather than a field, including pure-virtual, const, operator, and destructor forms; real data members stay fields (#3963, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: a Rust type used before it is declared in the same file now resolves to its local declaration instead of fabricating an external stub; resolution is a two-pass, order-independent scan, and a forward reference whose name collides with another same-id item is kept unresolved (fail-closed) (#3903, #3782, thanks @Yyunozor).
  • Fix: Rust prelude types (Option, Result, Vec, String, Box, Rc, Arc, HashMap, and friends) no longer accumulate spurious in-degree and surface as god nodes that distort community detection and ranking; they are filtered at extraction time, and a type the file defines itself is kept. Tuple-struct and unit-struct construction (ClientId(id)) is reclassified from a calls edge to a references/constructor edge (#3973, thanks @liam-mcelhaney122).
  • Fix: an Obsidian-style wikilink to a note whose name contains a dot ([[v1.2 release]], [[note.en]]) now resolves instead of being dropped by a premature extension strip; plain, explicit-extension, anchor, and alias wikilinks are unchanged, a literal indexed file beside the link keeps precedence, and a genuinely missing target is still not fabricated (#3905, #3904, thanks @Yyunozor).
  • Fix: a constructor call whose target is a same-file annotation stub (a source-less node minted by an earlier annotation or generic-argument reference) is kept for cross-file resolution and binds to the real definition when there is import or namespace/using-scope evidence, instead of being dropped; a genuinely external unresolved name is still not fabricated (#3901, thanks @bercedev).
  • Fix: the CLI hook-guard that protects graphify's own output directory now resolves paths and checks real containment instead of substring matching, so a sibling directory sharing a name prefix (artifacts/graphify-notes vs artifacts/graphify) is no longer wrongly treated as inside the output dir; symlinks, .., relative paths, and case-insensitive filesystems are handled (#3964, #3959, thanks @shobhitagnihotri69).
  • Fix: when resolving an import of a workspace package that ships both a source entry and a built dist, the graph now prefers the source file (so edges point at authored code) and falls back to the built artifact only when no source entry exists, generalizing the existing source-over-dist preference from the exports path to the legacy main/module fields (#4000, #3834, thanks @Adityakk9031).
  • Feature: Verilog header files (.vh) are now detected and extracted through the same tree-sitter-verilog grammar as .v/.sv, so macros, parameters, and modules declared in headers are captured (#3983, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
  • Fix: an incremental update no longer drops a hyperedge from an untouched file when a re-extracted file emits a hyperedge with the same id; carried hyperedges are now keyed by (id, source_file) so a same-id edge from a different, unchanged file is preserved while a genuine same-file re-emit still replaces (#3997, #3981, thanks @Ayushraj06-bit).
  • Feature: Kotlin class-literal references in annotation arguments (@ManyToOne(targetEntity = Customer::class)) are now extracted as attribute references to the referenced type (#3965, #3835, thanks @hopstreax).
  • Fix: Lua colon-method calls (obj:method(), self:method()) now resolve to the table-qualified method definition; a non-self receiver fails closed with no cross-file member fabrication (#3994, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Feature: Erlang local fun references (fun Name/Arity, as in lists:map(fun helper/1, L)) are now recorded as indirect_call edges to the arity-matched local function; remote fun Mod:Name/Arity and anonymous funs are left as-is, and an undefined or arity-mismatched local fails closed (#3996, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: C# null-conditional member calls (receiver?.Method()) now resolve through the same typed-receiver path as receiver.Method(), including the call-site generic-argument walk; chained and element-access forms fall through to bare-name resolution with no fabrication (#3976, #3797, thanks @Cintu07).

entry.title: v1.105.0-dev.2

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.0-dev.2

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.105.0-dev.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.105.0-dev.2

entry.title: Confidence Thresholds for Model Escalation Routing
entry.content: Confidence-based escalation keeps most requests on a cheap model and sends only the ones it is unsure about to a stronger one. This guide covers forcing a numeric confidence field with structured outputs, setting the threshold from error rates on your own traffic, tuning it against accuracy, cost, and latency, routing the escalation in your code, and re-tuning it after launch.

entry.title: Cost vs. Quality Tradeoff Framework for Agent Models
entry.content: The cheapest model that clears your quality bar is usually not the model at the top of a leaderboard. This framework sets the bar for one task, measures cost per quality point across a cheap, a mid-tier, and a frontier model on your own examples, and picks the cheapest one that clears the bar with margin. It uses live catalog prices and the cost each OpenRouter response reports.

entry.content: A one-line prompt change can ship an agent that tells customers the wrong refund window, and nothing in a normal CI pipeline checks what the model says. entry.title: v1.104.0-rc.2
entry.content:
Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-rc.2

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.104.0-rc.2/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.104.0-rc.2

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

entry.title: v0.9.72
entry.content:
• Feature: after a package upgrade, graphify refreshes stale installed skills automatically (the SKILL.md + references sidecar it manages) so the version-mismatch warning no longer requires a manual graphify install. It runs on any non-install CLI command when a skill is stale, backs up local edits to SKILL.md.bak, never touches your marker-bounded CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md sections, and can be disabled with GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 (#3895, #1805, thanks @bercedev).
  • Fix: graph.html's Node Info panel now shows the real Type/Source/Community for each node instead of "Type: unknown / Source: -" (the panel read field names that did not match the emitted node schema); aggregated community nodes show a member count (#3918, #3914, thanks @hopstreax).
  • Fix: a Kotlin class property that is both annotated and has an inferred type (@Volatile var x = 0) no longer crashes extraction with an UnboundLocalError that dropped the whole file (#3915, thanks @nothariharan; #3899, thanks @harshaygadekar; #3884).
  • Fix: SQL DDL that appears before a PostgreSQL DO $$ ... $$ block is now extracted — the block node the parser produces for that span is walked instead of skipped (#3900, thanks @bercedev).
  • Fix: Razor extracts C# members from @functions { } blocks (classic Razor Pages/MVC), not only Blazor @code { } blocks (#3908, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Feature: Blade templates now link a view to the layout it @extends (#3907, thanks @rajatnagda45).

entry.title: Desktop app, page narration, webhook-triggered automations, and more
entry.content:
Desktop app

  • Desktop app (beta): Use your dashboard and editor in a native app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Work in multiple tabs and windows, each with its own session. See Desktop app for more information and to download the app.

Editor

  • MDX checks in source mode: Source mode flags misspelled components, unknown or duplicate props, invalid prop values, missing required props, and unclosed tags. Hover over a flagged problem to apply a quick fix.
  • Autocomplete and hover definitions in source mode: Type < to get suggestions for components, props, and values, including page links, image paths, and icons. Hover over a component or prop to see its definition. See Visual and source mode.
  • Formatting in suggesting mode: In suggesting mode, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and inline code changes become suggestions that teammates can accept or reject. See Suggestions.
  • Granular publishing: The Selective publishing setting is now called Granular publishing. By default, the Publish menu shows and publishes only your own changes. Turn on granular publishing to also choose from changes your teammates made. See Granular publishing.
  • List and table shortcuts: Cmd + Shift + 7 creates a numbered list and Cmd + Shift + 9 creates a task list. Use Ctrl instead of Cmd on Windows and Linux. Type [] and a space to start a task list. Tab and Shift + Tab indent and outdent every selected list item. In tables, Tab moves to the next cell and adds a row from the last cell. See Keyboard shortcuts.
  • Copy and paste: Copying keeps the structure, numbering, and formatting of lists. Pasting from Google Docs keeps bold text and links in lists, and Google Docs checklists and GitHub task lists paste as task lists.
  • Comments: Unsent comment drafts survive page reloads, replies stay put when a thread collapses, and a comment can contain only a mention. See Comments.
  • Private page roles: The Publisher role for sharing private pages is now called Full Access. Permissions are unchanged. See Share a private page.
  • Files: The Hidden files section is now called Files and lists every file in your repository that isn't in your navigation. See Files.
  • Faster editor: Pages open faster, typing no longer reparses the whole page, and navigation loads without waiting on GitHub data. When you switch projects, the editor reopens the page you last had open.

Agent and assistant

  • Image reading: The editor agent can view JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP images on your pages to describe them, write alt text, or check screenshots against the surrounding content. The assistant can also inspect images on the pages it reads. See View images.
  • Agent panel: The editor agent panel has a new design, is faster in long chats, folds long messages, and lets you start typing from anywhere in the panel.
  • Links to new pages: When the agent creates pages, its final message links to each one.
  • Assistant exports: Assistant CSV exports list the sources each answer cited.

Automations

  • Webhook triggers: Start a custom automation with an authenticated POST request to its webhook URL, using an organization API key with write access. Each request runs the automation's saved prompt. See Trigger a webhook automation.
  • Multiple pull requests per run: A custom automation can open several pull requests in one run. When its prompt asks, it can also add changes to open pull requests from its earlier runs.
  • Managing automations: Editors can now delete automations and triggers link to their repositories and channels.

Published sites

  • Narration (beta): Readers can listen to a page from a Listen to this page player at the top of the page. Mintlify highlights each sentence as it plays and skips code blocks, tables, and other non-prose content. Turn on narration in your project settings. Each generation uses 50 credits. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans. See Narration.
  • WebMCP: Mintlify registers your site's MCP tools in the browser, so browsers and in-browser agents that support WebMCP can search and read your docs while someone visits your site. No setup required. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans. See WebMCP.
  • Folder-level metatags: Set metatags for every page in a folder with seo.paths in docs.json. Page frontmatter now overrides metatags set in docs.json. See SEO settings.
  • MCP on authenticated sites: Hosted MCP servers no longer return 403 errors on sites with authentication enabled, and MCP settings appear for every project that uses authentication. See Enable authenticated MCP.

Dashboard and deployments

  • Projects: The dashboard now calls your deployments Projects instead of Sites.
  • Workspace name: Change your workspace name in your organization settings. Your organization's slug stays the same.
  • Rollbacks for editors: Editors can now roll back a deployment, not just admins. Available on Enterprise plans.
  • Faster multi-repo updates: Deployments with multiple repositories rebuild only what changed instead of running a full update.
  • mint validate: The command no longer copies static files, so it uses less disk space in repositories with many images.

Bug fixes

  • Tables and lists: HTML tables no longer lose rows on save, ordered lists in table cells keep their starting number, and task lists written with [X] no longer fail MDX validation.
  • Editor: New page titles keep focus while you type, pasted dollar amounts no longer turn into math, image paste works on new private pages, and the editor shows clearer errors when a repository was renamed, can't be accessed, or is blocked by a GitHub IP allowlist.
  • Publishing: Publishing works around navigation errors instead of blocking, the editor rejects publish selections and docs.json edits that would drop navigation entries, and the publish button no longer gets stuck.
  • Published sites: Related pages render in preview deployments, locale redirects work behind proxies and custom base paths, breadcrumb groups without a root page render as text instead of a broken link, shell placeholders highlight correctly, and SDK type references link to their generated pages.
  • Search: Results from other versions show their version breadcrumb again.
  • Deployments: Mintlify removes stale OpenAPI pages when a spec changes.
  • Invites: Invite links work for users who are already logged in.

entry.title: v0.9.68
entry.content:
• Security: the /graphify add ... --watch reference no longer passes the raw, agent-substituted INPUT_PATH placeholder unquoted into a shell command (… -m graphify.watch INPUT_PATH), where a scan root containing $(…), backticks, or ; could execute — a follow-on to the Step 1 fix. The watcher now reads the trusted graphify-out/.graphify_root that Step 1 resolves, so there is no path to substitute (#3742, #3642, thanks @ayushcodes10). The identical placeholder still appears in the Aider/Devin monolith --watch snippet and is tracked separately.
  • Fix: incremental updates (update/extract --code-only/watch) now preserve a cross-file imports/calls/uses edge whose target symbol lives in an unchanged file — the symbol-resolution facts pass widens its target index with the read-only resolution context, so re-extracting one file no longer silently drops its edges into the rest of the graph; a genuinely removed edge is still pruned (#3812, #3776, thanks @hopstreax).
  • Fix: C# type references (inherits/implements/parameter/return/base types) no longer resolve to a same-named non-type node — an enum member, property, field, or method sharing a type's name is excluded from the type-definition index, so a class inherits from the real base rather than a stray member; resolution of partial classes without a contains edge is restored (#3815, #3795, thanks @hopstreax).
  • Fix: dedup now keeps the node with a real source location over a richer but source-less one when merging duplicates, so a merged entity points at real code instead of an inferred/external stub; the loser's attributes are still folded onto the survivor (#3786, #3775, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: Maven pom.xml ingestion resolves a dependency's inherited groupId/version from the local <parent> block and substitutes ${property} / ${project.*} placeholders (offline, one level), so previously-dangling depends_on edges now connect (#3823, #3806, thanks @chiliec).
  • Fix: the PYTHONHASHSEED re-exec (0.9.67) now waits for and propagates the child's exit code on Windows instead of returning early — os.execvpe is a true process replacement only on POSIX; on Windows it spawned a new process and let the parent race ahead unpinned, crashing update/extract/cluster-only/label. The Windows path now spawns via subprocess.run and exits with the child's status; the POSIX path is unchanged (#3816, #3799, thanks @sinangumuskabak-sys).
  • Fix: Terraform secret redaction now also covers a secret-named variable default and output value — the secret's name lives in the block label, so the literal sat under the generic default/value key that the key-name check never flagged (variable "db_password" { default = "…" } reached graph.json verbatim). Redacted when the label names a secret or the block sets sensitive = true (#3817, #3644/#3762 follow-up, thanks @breken-ai).
  • Fix: fixed-format COBOL that carries a sequence NUMBER in columns 1-6 (not blanks) is now detected as fixed-format — previously it was misread as free-format, the sequence digits stayed in the code, and every paragraph and PERFORM edge was silently dropped, leaving only the file and program nodes (#3813, thanks @abhay-codes07).
  • Fix: PERFORM A THRU/THROUGH Z now links both endpoints of the range, not just the entry paragraph, so the range-end no longer lacks an inbound calls edge; a dangling THRU target is skipped rather than fabricated (#3814, thanks @abhay-codes07).
  • Fix: GRAPH_REPORT.md's Knowledge Gaps section only offers "undocumented components" as an explanation for an isolated node when the graph actually has a semantic layer (a document/paper/image node an LLM extracted meaning from) — a code-only graph no longer lists a possibility it can never have (#3828, #3801, thanks @ayushcodes10).

entry.content:
• Feature: five new language extractors — COBOL (.cbl/.cob/.cobol/.cpy; programs, paragraphs, PERFORM/CALL/COPY, pure-regex, no new dependency) (#3713, thanks @Abdul535), VB.NET (.vb; case-insensitive types/methods, Inherits/Implements/Handles) (#3717, thanks @Abdul535), R (.r/.R; assignment-form function defs, library/source, S4/R6 classes) (#3715, thanks @Abdul535), Solidity (.sol; contracts/interfaces/libraries, is inheritance, imports, modifiers) (#3716, thanks @Abdul535), and Erlang (.erl/.hrl/.escript; modules, functions by arity, behaviours, local + remote foo:bar() calls) (#3714, thanks @Abdul535). The R and Erlang grammars ship via the r/erlang extras (they have no standalone PyPI wheel); Solidity and VB.NET have their own extras.
  • Feature: Go interface method requirements now resolve to the interface, and their parameter/return types emit references edges (#3672, #3737, thanks @rajatnagda45, @oleksii-tumanov).
  • Feature: a Rust self.method() call resolves across files for simple generic impls (impl<T> Foo<T>) (#3653, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
  • Fix: graph.json is now deterministic across runs — update/extract/cluster-only/label pin PYTHONHASHSEED via a one-time re-exec, so hash-seed-sensitive community detection (Leiden/Louvain) produces identical output run-to-run and matches hook-triggered rebuilds (#3743, #3641, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: a same-relation edge collision now keeps the higher-confidence edge (EXTRACTED over INFERRED) instead of resolving by arrival order (#3711, thanks @shobhitagnihotri69).
  • Fix: a spec-conformant method-node duplicate (dropped class segment / leading dot) is now deduplicated onto its canonical AST node, gated on a method-shaped label and a single unambiguous candidate (#3719, #3705, thanks @shobhitagnihotri69).
  • Fix: intra-module Go imports_from edges now repoint onto the imported package's real file nodes instead of dangling at a go_pkg_ sink; external/stdlib imports stay external (#3748, thanks @carterko23).
  • Fix: Cargo introspection discovers a Cargo.toml in a subdirectory when none sits at the scan root (e.g. Tauri's src-tauri/), degrades gracefully instead of aborting the whole extraction when no manifest is found, and resolves workspace = true inherited dependency identity from [workspace.dependencies] (#3740, #3739, thanks @ayushcodes10; #3734, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
  • Fix: MCP get_node/get_neighbors now accept the node identifier under node_id/id, not only label, so agents that spell the argument differently no longer get a missing-argument error (#3725, thanks @ahm3dwasim).
  • Fix: graphify install no longer corrupts line endings (writes preserve the file's existing EOLs instead of rewriting to CRLF on Windows) and re-install is properly idempotent (a marker-bounded replace instead of a bare substring check) (#3741, #3668, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: community labeling retries a valid-but-truncated LLM response and reports how many communities kept a structural fallback name, instead of silently leaving them unlabeled (#3708, thanks @Ha1baraA11).
  • Fix: a stale .graphify_root marker (moved/deleted/symlink-loop target) is now ignored with a fall-back to the graph's directory, and the marker value resolves to an absolute path when GRAPHIFY_OUT is a shared absolute directory (#3707, thanks @Ha1baraA11; #3735, #3375, thanks @ayushcodes10).

entry.title: Scoped automation triggers, editor agent integrations, and more
entry.content:
Automations

  • Scoped GitHub triggers: Custom automations can now trigger on GitHub topics and filter to paths and specific authors.
  • GitHub topic search: When you configure a repository-topic trigger, Mintlify suggests topics from your organization's repositories so you can pick one without leaving the settings page.
  • Automatic merge conflict resolution: Automations now resolve merge conflicts on their own pull requests without needing you to open the PR first. See Resolve merge conflicts.
  • Automations menu: A new Automations menu in the dashboard topbar links to your automations, runs, and settings. Sidebar automation cards show a live count of runs that need review.
  • Runs tab improvements: The Runs tab now shows a preview deployment link and lets you open a run in the editor, view run details, or edit the automation's settings.

Editor agent

  • Connected integrations as tools: The agent can call your connected third-party apps while researching and editing. The agent can prompt you to connect a new integration when it needs one.
  • Roll back edits: Ask the agent to undo a change and it reverts the pages it edited in the current session.
  • Current page context: The agent now sees the page you have open and its unsaved edits, so requests like "fix this section" apply to what you are working on.

Editor collaboration

  • @mentions: Type @ in a page to mention a teammate. Mentioned teammates get a notification.
  • Profile picture uploads: Upload a profile picture from your account settings. It appears on comments, mentions, and collaborator avatars.
  • Workspace folder icons: Edit the icon on a workspace folder from its menu. Folder metadata is preserved when you move or rename it.
  • Emoji favicons: A new Emojis tab in the icon picker lets you set an emoji as a page icon, and emoji icons render as the editor tab favicon.
  • Reorder shared and starred pages: Drag pages in Shared with me and Starred to set the order you want. The order syncs across your devices.
  • Version history redesign: The version history panel has a refreshed layout that's easier to scan when comparing revisions.
  • Faster editor rendering: Visual mode renders, switches pages, and scrolls faster.

Dashboard

  • Rebuilt Activity page: The Activity page has a new layout and shows richer details.
  • SSO login route: A new login route detects SSO configuration for your email domain and sends you to the right identity provider. The SSO connection limit is raised to 25.
  • Assistant layout settings: Deployment settings include options for the assistant layout so you can control how the assistant appears on your published site.

Analytics

  • Sort and export improvements: Page ratings support sort order, feedback shows the page URL, and assistant analytics exports include feedback ratings.
  • Page filter polish: The page filter opens on the currently selected page, resets with the clear button, and shows All pages as the default label.
  • Page-scoped popular pages, referrals, and top agents: These analytics widgets accept a page filter so you can drill into a single page.

Published sites

  • Related pages on authenticated sites: Related pages now appear on sites protected by Mintlify authentication.
  • Copy assistant responses: Select text and copy full responses from the assistant.

Bug fixes

  • Editor publishing: Pending edits are saved before publishing, deleted page titles show in the publish panel, publish retries when the branch lock is held, GitHub same-path replaces succeed, GitLab create collisions no longer break publish, and rows the server keeps after publish are preserved.
  • Editor: Language switcher options are disabled for pages without a translation, new page paths update until the first commit, slash commands rank by relevance, frontmatter edits are preserved during Git sync, source-mode comments no longer show false conflicts, and the page title is preserved across navigation.
  • Automations: Folder selection and topic search work correctly in the create flow, automatic conflict resolution skips mandatory PR mode when needed, and the trigger options popover collapses cleanly.
  • OpenAPI and API playground: Reverse-proxy guides render for sites with a base path, schema validation errors stay on one line, and locally-ignored OpenAPI specs are marked stale on full updates.
  • Client and hosting: RSS URLs no longer duplicate base paths, custom and frame pages render without a layout shift on load, and color swatches pick their theme value in CSS.

  • Fixed credits for assistant answers: Each assistant answer uses 25 credits.
  • Fixed automation pricing: All automations use 250 credits per successful run. If an automation fails or finds nothing to update, it uses zero credits.
  • Free editor and Slack agent: Using the agent in the editor or Slack does not use credits for Pro and Enterprise plans.

OpenAPI Overlays

  • Transform a spec: Use OpenAPI Overlays to rename paths, replace server URLs, or remove internal endpoints without editing the specification file. Overlays apply after a specification is parsed and before it is validated, so generated endpoint pages, navigation, openapi frontmatter, and mint validate all use the transformed document. See Transform your spec with overlays.
  • Overlay Specification 1.0 and 1.1: Write update, remove, and copy actions that select nodes with RFC 9535 JSONPath expressions. See Create an overlay document.
  • Reference or auto-discover overlays: Add an overlays property anywhere your docs.json accepts openapi, using a relative path or a URL. Or skip the configuration: an overlay with an extends field pointing at your specification is discovered automatically. See Auto-discover overlays.

Editor and collaboration

  • Recent and starred private pages: The Workspace tab of the editor now lists the private pages you opened most recently and the ones you star from a page's menu. Both lists sync across your devices and stay the same on every branch. Each section stays hidden until it has something in it. You can reorder these sidebar groups by dragging them to create your preferred workspace layout.
  • Move and duplicate private pages: Move a private page into a workspace folder from its document or sidebar menu, duplicate a private page from the same menu, or leave a private page you were invited to. When you promote a private page, its images and videos move with it and inline references are rewritten. See Private pages.
  • Comments panel: Open a document-wide comments panel to review open and resolved threads for the current page. Source mode now supports comments the same as visual mode. See Comments.
  • Resize table columns: In visual mode, drag a column border to resize it. The editor converts the table to HTML and writes the <colgroup> widths for you. See Tables.
  • Site settings in the sidebar: Site configuration pages open directly from the editor sidebar instead of a modal, and workspace settings navigation has been reorganized to match.
  • Page icons as tab favicons: The editor tab favicon now uses the page's icon. Page and navigation icon frontmatter accept emoji values.

Automations

  • Automatic merge conflict resolution: When an automation's pull request has merge conflicts, the agent can resolve them for you, either automatically or when you click Accept on the pull request. See Resolve merge conflicts.
  • Manual pull request runs: Manually triggered runs against a specific pull request are now labeled as such in the runs feed, and the runs page shows run count badges, unified result cards, and a simpler summary. See Manage automations.

Published sites

  • Image viewer: Clicking an image opens a rebuilt full-size viewer with smoother animation and labeled controls for screen readers.
  • Search ranking: Search ranks page-title matches higher, so exact-title lookups surface first.

Dashboard

  • Workspace and organization icons: Upload a workspace icon from your general settings and an organization icon from your organization settings. See Change your workspace icon.
  • IP-blocked error page: Requests blocked by an IP allowlist now land on a dedicated error page that explains what happened.

Git and integrations

  • Non-Markdown files sync in the editor: Editor branches now sync non-MDX text files, so changes to config files and other plain-text assets round-trip through the editor.
  • GitLab editor branches: GitLab pushes sync into editor branches in real time, contributors show on the branch dropdown, and force pushes are detected. Git-only branches now appear in the editor branch dropdown so you can switch to a branch that was created outside the editor.
  • Editor branch dropdown: The branch dropdown is now a per-user editor setting. Turn it on from your editor settings to switch branches from the editor.
  • Default ignored patterns: .vscode and .cursor are ignored by default, and mint dev skips ignored directories when it crawls your project. See Default ignored patterns.

API playground

  • Playground labels: The oneOf variant dropdown uses title-aware labels so each option is easier to identify.

Bug fixes

  • Preview deployments: GitHub preview deployments are pinned to the triggering commit, preview URLs stay stable across rebuilds, and preview comments refresh after each rebuild.
  • Custom domains and 404s: Custom hostnames Cloudflare no longer serves return not_found, MCP analytics resolve custom domains to their canonical subdomain, and Markdown 404s include recovery guidance and discovery headers.
  • Components: RequestExample and ResponseExample code blocks no longer disappear on small screens.
  • Editor fixes: Creating a branch no longer leaves a stuck skeleton, pull-request link redirects no longer double-encode branch names, saving rows match the server, resizing no longer loops, and frontmatter loads only after the document connects.
  • Publishing: Content-less create actions retire after publish so they cannot block later publishes, publish retries when the branch lock is held instead of erroring immediately, and GitHub commit failures report clearer messages.
  • Dashboard fixes: SSO configuration resets when you remove a connection, only verified domains can be selected when SSO is configured, and the page header restores the Add description affordance.
  • Auth and account: Password reset is asynchronous and rate limited, dev org rate limits are raised, and a new-account flag lets the dashboard fire the correct sign-up event.
  • OpenAPI: Memory usage during OpenAPI candidate detection is reduced, API reference pages slice the schema graph to the page's target, and $ref prefixes and array entries resolve correctly in overlays under base paths and mounts.

Notification preferences

  • Share notifications: Mintlify notifies you when someone shares a page with you.

Editor and collaboration

  • Collaborative source mode: Source mode now supports real-time collaboration. See your teammates' cursors as they work on the same branch as you. Frontmatter edits sync live across visual and source mode. See Real-time editing.
  • Comment reactions: React to a comment with an emoji to acknowledge it without replying. Hover over a reaction to see who reacted, and reacting to someone else's comment notifies its author. See Comments.
  • Selective publish: Select individual changes in the publish menu to publish part of your pending work instead of everything at once.
  • Media on private pages: Upload images and videos to private pages. Private media is served only to people who can open the page, and it is removed when the page is deleted.
  • Editor polish: Search results show page titles and reveal the file in the sidebar, the sidebar lists only Markdown pages by default, the share dialog searches recipients by email address, the emoji suggestion menu has better search relevance, and the agent panel stays available in site settings.

Automations

  • Run scope for manual runs: When you trigger an automation manually, choose whether it reviews changes since a date, the entire site, or a specific pull request. See Run an automation manually.

Analytics

  • Page filter: Filter your analytics to a specific page with the new page dropdown in the dashboard.

API playground

  • Optional field toggles: In the playground modal, required fields sort first and optional fields collapse behind an Expand N optional fields control, with a global toggle in the header. Collapsed fields stay findable. Searching the page for a hidden field name expands the section that contains it, and values you entered persist across collapse and expand.
  • Collapse fields by default: Set expand: false under x-mint: playground on an operation to collapse nested object fields by default. See Collapse playground fields.

Authoring

  • mint test: Generate tests for the code blocks in your docs from the CLI. Runs are saved so you can revisit past reports. See mint test.
  • <MDX> improvements: Headings inside <MDX> blocks merge into the page's table of contents, ## Title {#id} anchors work at any indent, and code blocks inside <MDX> behave like code blocks at the page root. See MDX.
  • Markdown in component titles: Component titles, such as accordion titles, support inline Markdown formatting like code and bold.

Referrals

Bug fixes

Editor and collaboration

  • Editor branches: When you create a branch, the editor now creates a draft pull request and autosaves changes to Git. You can rename or delete branches, discard autosaved changes, and move pending changes to a new branch. The branch menu is ordered by recent activity, uses per-user branch names, and shows cleaner Draft <date> names for automatically generated branches. See Branching and publishing.
  • Pull requests open as drafts by default: The editor now opens new pull requests in draft state so you can share a preview URL without signaling that the change is ready to merge. Change this on the editor settings page.
  • GitLab merge requests: Merge requests opened in GitLab now sync into editor branches, matching the existing GitHub behavior.
  • Streamlined editor navigation: The editor has a new breadcrumbs row, consolidated page and share controls, sticky sidebar section headers, and a dedicated bottom bar for settings and Ask agent. Site settings open as editor pages instead of a modal. Mobile navigation now uses a simplified top bar and panel-based sidebar for smaller screens.
  • Page access and comments: Request edit access to a private or protected page from the editor and review requests in an approval modal. Comment cards now show profile pictures, and @mentions link to the mentioned user.
  • Duplicate private pages: Duplicate a private page from the editor to start a new draft from existing content.
  • Live preview improvements: Run multiple local previews at once. Navigation changes now propagate to open previews, the agent panel docks on the left, and the preview remains visible during onboarding follow-up turns.

Automations and integrations

  • Slack message trigger: Enterprise customers can run custom automations from new messages in selected Slack channels. The agent evaluates each message and takes action only when warranted. See Trigger an automation from an integration.
  • Redesigned automations page: The automations list has a new layout, and each automation card shows its run count and who created it. See Manage automations.

Docs and delivery

  • Custom SDK reference pages: Use sdk frontmatter to generate documentation for a single SDK symbol while adding your own examples or guidance above it. You can also configure SDK generation for a navigation group. See Customize a page for a single symbol.
  • GraphQL input types: Input type pages are now generated and served on GraphQL API reference sites. See GraphQL setup.
  • nocopy code blocks: Add the nocopy flag to a fenced code block to hide its copy button. For plain-text content such as ASCII diagrams, use a bare nocopy fence. See Hide copy button.
  • Result snippets: Optionally show a one-line content preview beneath each search result, with matching terms highlighted. Enable Result snippets from your dashboard search settings; the setting is off by default. See Result snippets.
  • Scoped llms.txt indexes: Grouped llms.txt indexes are now served per URL segment at /_llms/<segment>.md, so agents can pull one section of your docs instead of the full index.
  • Assistant widget analytics: Analytics events now include the embedding page's current pathname by default and follow client-side navigation. Set analytics.capturePathname to false to opt out. See assistant analytics config.
  • Bulk member invites: Invite up to 250 teammates at once, then review the list and assign a role to each invitee before sending. Pro and Enterprise plans can upload a CSV of email addresses. See Add members to your organization.
  • Universal Search API keys: Universal Search API keys are out of early access. Any organization can now create and manage them from dashboard settings.
  • Analytics in self-hosted deployments: The dashboard analytics tab is now available on self-hosted deployments.

Bug fixes

  • API playground: OpenAPI 3.1 examples and enum values now appear in generated response samples, and Markdown lists in the endpoint modal no longer render double bullets.
  • Search anchors: JSX headings with custom IDs now create the correct search sections and anchors.
  • Inline styles: Inline CSS in a quoted style attribute now renders correctly on your site, in the CLI, and in the editor.
  • Editor components: Copying and pasting inside a Step no longer creates nested steps, tabs no longer jump when clicked, and settings sidebar search has been restored.
  • Editor deep links: Opening an editor link while signed out now returns you to that page after login instead of the dashboard home page.
  • Anchor icons: Anchor link icons remain white when hovering over a dark background.
  • Assistant widget loading: The widget stays interactive while it's loading.
  • Docs MCP: Unknown tool calls now return a JSON-RPC error instead of failing silently, and MCP tool schemas use the 2020-12 JSON Schema dialect.

Bitbucket Cloud support

Editor and collaboration

  • Editor autocommits: Turn on autocommits in the editor settings to commit your work as you type.

  • Private pages: Private pages have their own version history, agent annotations, and notification emails. Move a private page to a workspace folder to publish it to your site.
  • Personal and shared sections: The editor sidebar has Personal and Shared sections so private drafts and shared content are easier to separate.
  • Editor comments: Long comment bodies clamp to six lines with a Show more control, and the comment card scrolls, keyboard shortcuts, and edit input have been polished.

  • Collaborators in branches: The branches dropdown shows collaborators on each branch, avatars dedupe across Git and editor identities, and pull request authors are included in the contributors list. External pushes to editor branches sync into the editor in real time.

Docs and delivery

  • GitHub component: Embed a public GitHub repository card with a live description, star count, and fork count on any page. See GitHub for usage and variants.
  • Language-preference routing: Redirect visitors from the root of your site to the language that matches their browser's Accept-Language header. Enable Auto-route to preferred language on the Add-ons page. See Navigation for details.
  • lastUpdatedDate frontmatter: The last-modified footer now prefers a lastUpdatedDate value in a page's frontmatter over the Git commit date.
  • Search relevance: Verbatim identifier matches are promoted in search results, and identifier tokens are preserved across chunk splits.
  • Translation reliability: Full-site translation triggers are fixed, and the translation timeout is raised to accommodate larger sites.
  • API playground endpoint menu: Refined layout and spacing, correct column sizing for OPTIONS, and typing in the endpoint search is fixed.

Agent integrations

  • Stripe and expanded Notion integrations: Connect Stripe as a read-only integration, and use additional Notion read tools in Slack and automations.
